proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: We met after I closed the bookshop, six Thursdays in a row, at the table in the back. Each time I went home with one page and one thing to do. By the fifth week I had stopped dreading the mail.
reviews.name: Hollis B.

reviews.text: The cash calendar showed me the March gap in January. I moved a supplier payment and asked two wholesale accounts to pay on delivery. Payroll cleared the whole winter.
reviews.name: Ines V.

reviews.text: I had not changed my prices since I opened the bike shop. Ruth sat with my old invoices and worked out what a tune-up really costs me. I raised it, posted the new sheet, and nobody blinked.
reviews.name: Teddy K.

reviews.text: Our farm stand went year-round and suddenly we had eight people and no idea who was in charge of what. We came out with three written roles and a schedule my sister and I both agreed to.
reviews.name: Marguerite D.

reviews.text: Practical, a bit blunt, and never once used a word I had to look up. The homework was real homework though.
reviews.name: Calvin O.

reviews.text: I am the only one who knew how to do the wholesale orders. Now there is a binder with photos of each step, and I took my first full week off in four years in August.
reviews.name: Priya S.

proof.guarantee: If the first session isn't useful to you, you don't pay for it.
